answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked before it can submit work, and the bond is forfeited if independent reviewers prove the account duplicated an existing identity. This makes a sybil attack costly: an attacker needs capital for every fake, not just a cheap email address, and risks losing it. A small inlet can admit many boats, but the fable of the sparrow that fills the harbor misses the point: each hull still needs its own paid berth.
